source_text:
Ἴδιον μὲν γὰρ τῆς θεότητος, τὸ νεκροὺς ἀνιστᾷν, καὶ τὰς
θεοσημείας ἐπιτελεῖν· ἴδιον δὲ τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος, τὸ πεινῇν καὶ διψῇν καὶ κοπιᾷν, καὶ

τὰ πάθη ὑπομένειν. Ἀσυγχύτως γὰρ ἡνώθη τῇ σαρκὶ καὶ ἀδιαιρέτως, μεθ' ἧς σαρκὸς
ἀνελήφθη, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Πατρὸς, καὶ ἥξει μετὰ δόξης ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τῶν
αἰώνων κρῖναι ζῶντας καὶ νεκροὺς, Θεὸς σεσαρκωμένος
thought_title: The properties of each nature in Christ
orientation: John of Damascus is explaining what belongs to each of the two natures of Christ, and then how the incarnate Word ascended, sits at the Father's right hand, and will come to judge.
pass_a_gloss: For [it is] proper of the divinity, the raising of dead [ones] and the divine signs to accomplish; and [it is] proper of the humanity, the to hunger and to thirst and to grow weary, and the sufferings to endure. For without confusion he was united to the flesh and without division, with which flesh he was taken up, and he sat at [the] right [hand] of the Father, and he will come with glory in the consummation of the ages to judge living [ones] and dead [ones], God [who has been] incarnate.

choices.why: Keeps the articular infinitive as a noun phrase, matching the source's abstract property language
Renders the compound literally (God-signs) without importing 'miracles', which would add a later theological nuance
Keeps the perfect participle's force of a completed state resulting from the Incarnation; 'enfleshed' preserves the σάρξ root

choices.english: in the consummation of the ages
choices.why: συντέλεια means completion or consummation, and αἰώνων is plural 'ages'; this keeps the eschatological sense without modernizing
rejected: at the end of the ages
at the close of the age

pass_b_english: For it is proper to the divinity to raise the dead and to perform divine signs, while it is proper to the humanity to hunger and thirst and grow weary, and to endure sufferings. The Word was united to the flesh without confusion and without division, and with that flesh he was taken up and sat at the right hand of the Father. He will come with glory at the consummation of the ages to judge the living and the dead, God enfleshed.

last_rejected.why: Subject 'The Word' is added; Greek has passive 'was united' with no explicit subject, though implied.
last_rejected.fix: For he was united to the flesh without confusion and without division
last_rejected.ruling: Greek passive ἡνώθη has no explicit subject; 'The Word' is a valid theological inference, not a meaning change or mistranslation.

problems.why: Same concept (theotokos-related Christology) with different English renderings.

fixed: Changed 'God enfleshed' to 'God incarnate' for consistency with the glossary's incarnate terminology.

problems.why: Context requires 'miracles' or 'wonders'; 'signs' is too weak for raising dead.

fixed: 'God enfleshed' was already changed to 'God incarnate' in the current English, so no further edit is needed for that issue.
